Lowveld Tourism Under Threat

By: Stenette Grosskopf | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Tourism in our iconic Mpumalanga Lowveld is under threat!

Unique Selling Point:
The issue has largely been kept out of the media but there are daily service delivery protests in the Ehlanzeni District Municipality area (basically the entire Lowveld region), threatening the livelihood of tourism in this area. Specifically, the Thaba Chweu Local Municipality has a bad reputation when it comes to service delivery (according to locals). So locals are barricading the scenic routes and access roads to major tourist attractions which means that tourism operators have to make last-minute changes to their itineraries and self-drive tourists are affected on a daily basis.

Locals are protesting poor (or non-existent) service delivery. Outside Mbombela a community was hard hit by a hail storm and the repairs have not been done completely. Resident are angry and keep barricading the N4 and other major routes outside the city.
Near Hazyview, communities are protesting lack of water and electricity. Some people were given RDP housing, but there has been no water or electricity connections and the community is fed-up. It's been 3 years now. So, hence the frustrations. Similarly Graskop communities are also desperate for water and sanitation services and they are barricading roads leading to the iconic God's Window.

The whole area is plaqued by protests, but it is not one specific issue... The problem lies, it seems with the local and district municipalities and their total lack of service delivery. Schools are falling apart, hospitals are substandard, roads have massive potholes. Tourism is not the target per se, but it is one sector of business that is suffering greatly at the moment.
Another opinion comes from the African National Chamber of Commerce & Industry Mpumalanga -- saying that politicians with ambitions have seen the opportunity and are instigating the protests. He says the protests are well organised and are as a result of the in-fighting between various factions within the ANC that want control over the province.

Summary:
It is labelled as one of South Africa's most scenic areas. The Lowveld & Panorama Route of Mpumalanga showcases the natural awe inspiring areas of the district including God’s Window, Mac Mac Falls, Bourke’s Luck potholes, Kruger National Park and others. The area falls under the Ehlanzeni district municipality which encompasses four local municipalities -- Thaba Chweu, Bushbuckridge, City of Mbombela & Nkomazi. The entire area is affected by what started as locals protesting poor service delivery, and which has now escalated in to a more organised form of disruption with the aim of... no one knows for sure. Whilst National Government sees the area's tourism potential, the breakdown seems to be with local municipalities not coming to the party. But poor service delivery in the area has left local residents frustrated and they have now taken to daily protests, blockading the major scenic routes in the area, cutting off access to some of the tourist attractions. Although tourism is not the sole focus, many local tourism establishments that cater especially for international visitors are feeling the pressure as they have reported a decline in bookings (30 to 45%) over the past year. At least 2 international tourism operators are considering halting trips to the area for fear of safety, and because of the daily struggle to get tourists to and from Kruger National Park and airports, and other tourist destinations. Even roads to airports are affected. We speak to local accommodation owners and tourism operators about their daily frustrations and the disappointment of tourists when they are unable to visit the area's jewels.

The roads affected seem to be the ones that lead to the major tourist destinations, eg entry to Kruger National Park, Burke's Luck, Graskop and even the Adventura Resort. Locals burn tyres, and barricade the roads with branches and rocks.



Further information:
On 2nd July 2018, UNESCO declared the Barberton-Makhonjwa Mountainlands as South Africa's 10th World Heritage Site and Mpumalanga’s first! And on Friday 24 August Minister Derek Hanekom will open the new Graskop Gorge Lift in an ongoing effort to boost tourism in the Panorama Route area of the Lowveld, however whilst government and many local tourism organisations are serious about the region's tourism potential and the income it generates, the success of the region's tourism is hampered by a lack of service delivery from the local municipalities. Residents are protesting poor service delivery and various on-going issues on a daily basis in the area and this is affecting tourism throughout the region.

Ehlanzeni District Municipality (EDM) is one of the three districts in Mpumalanga Province and is located in the Northern Eastern part covering the whole Southern part of the Kruger National Park. EDM covers an area of 27 895.47 km² which is about (36.47%) of the 76 495 km² which is the total estimated land size of Mpumalanga Province.

The Thaba Chweu local municipality encompasses towns like Graskop, Pilgrims Rest and Sabie. Besides macadamia nut and citrus farming, tourism is the main source of income for many.

South Africa has been named the top Adventure Tourism Destination for 2018, and Mpumalanga, Kruger and the Panorama route features strongly on the SA Tourism menu (after Cape Town). The area offers many activities for the adventure seeking tourist, from safari's at one of the many private, provincial or national reserves, abseiling, quadbiking, hiking, river rafting... the list goes on and on.
National Accommodation Association of South Africa chair, Rosemarie van Staden says the area is feeling the pressure from cancellations by tourists and especially international tourism operators. It is not just the isolated B&B that is suffering. The whole region's economy is under threat.

The Kruger Lowveld Chamber of Business and Tourism is concerned about the effect on all businesses if tourism would to dry up.
The area is also becoming a crime hotspot. There are incidents of rock throwing at cars and people being attacked of threatened on some of the smaller roads.

Protests outside Mbombela -- KaNyamazane -- started when RDP houses (about 35) were damaged by hail. The contractor hired by the municipality to fix the roofs of the houses affected was the first point of contention. Residents claim the process was not above board. Then once the contractor completed the repairs of 10 houses, their invoice to the City of Mbombela was R90,000 per roof, instead of the R45,000 estimated. The city refused to pay and the contractor stopped work. Locals were angry and started protesting. However, then things changed and a list of other (older) grievances were added to their list of demands. The mayor visited the area and tried to speak to the community and was chased away. Then the MEC of the province visited and was chased away. Insiders point to a more sinister cause behind the ongoing protests. Key politicians within the ANC are said to instigate communities into protesting, in an effort to win political ground. It's a fight between different factions within the ANC, fighting for control of the province... or so say insiders.

In the meantime the entire Lowveld business community is struggling and desperate to find a way forward.

Script:


LOWVELD TOURISM UNDER THREAT



LINK
This is the Mpumalanga Lowveld, known for it's forestry, agriculture like citrus and macadamia and of course it's tourism.
V/O
The Lowveld is served by the District Municipality of Ehlanzeni that covers four local municipalities – its seat is Mbombela.

Tourists come for the iconic Kruger National Park, private game reserves and the Panorama Route that include jewels like Bourke's Luck Potholes, the Blyde River Canyon and God's Window.
Lisa Sheard
Tourism is very important to Mpumalanga and especially in our region, which is the Kruger/Lowveld-Ehlanzeni region, which contributes about 54% of the tourism GDP to Mpumalanga.
V/O
An estimated 1,5 million foreign tourists visited the province in 2017, says the executive director for tourism at the Kruger Lowveld Chamber of Business and Tourism, Lisa Sheard.
Lisa Sheard
Our primary markets are the traditional international markets like the UK, Germany.. the US is also a big market. So, a traditional South African inbound international market that visit our area.
LINK
This is God's Window. Tourists come from all over the world flock to come see this glorious splendour. Now imagine travelling all this way and getting to Graskop and not being able to get here because the road is blocked.
V/o
The entire Lowveld has been affected by service delivery protests. Roads have been blocked with branches, rocks and burning tyres. Dissatisfaction over poor service delivery lies at the heart of the unrest.
Since the beginning of the year the frequency of protests has escalated, with demonstrators barricading roads along the scenic Panorama route, preventing residents and tourists from accessing places like Hazyview, the Blyde River Canyon, various local airports, and even the Kruger National Park.
Eva Wagner
Tourism is under attack at the moment... It's not just two or three vehicles that couldn't get to the Panorama, the whole industry has been affected from the bottom right up.
V/O
Eva Wagner owns a local one-stop tourism service that represents more than thirty operators and promotes over a hundred different activities in the area. Everyone has been impacted by the protests.
Eva Wagner
These are desperate measures. These people just don't know where to go anymore, they have found that if they protest in this way somebody will come and listen to them.
LINK
Service delivery protests here in Ka-Nyamazane just outside Mbombela started earlier this year after a hailstorm caused extensive damage to approximately 2000 houses. Three months later and the area is still dotted with blue plastic sheeting that's on top of the houses that still need to be fixed.
V/O
After first agreeing to be interviewed, activist leaders and community representatives withdrew their participation, but the Provincial Head of the Human Settlements department agreed to explain the background to the residents’ dissatisfaction.
Kebone Masange
Just over 2,000 houses were affected and most of them were asbestos houses which were roofed with asbestos,... And then those that were severely damaged, I'm talking about those that were huge openings and all that, there were about 450.

CLAIRE: Right now, today, how many houses have been repaired? Do we have a number.

Yes, we, we, have. The reports that I have is that 240 houses so far have been repaired.
V/o
What started out as protests about hail-damaged houses has escalated into something bigger over the last few months.
Although the City of Mbombela has made funds available to assist, and the Provincial Government is on target to repair the worst-affected houses by the end of September, it seems promises are not enough to keep protests at bay.
Kebone Masange
But as you know the issues of employment and all that they are so much in our communities and people are actually scrambling for fewer job opportunities and work opportunities that come into this place. And due to that you end up having various interests playing in, and those who are not, disgruntled who are not chosen by this person... feeling like they've been sidelined. But that happens everywhere you go. Then unfortunately as a department we're not able to control that unless it comes up and then we intervene to try and cool temperatures and make the situation normal.

Protest action across the Lowveld has a far-reaching impact. BJ Nobunga is the the CEO of the Mpumalanga Tourism and Parks Agency, or MTPA which coordinates tourism promotion in the Province – a responsibility that begins with local government.
Boy Johannes Nobunga
Service delivery has turned into something which is common in South Africa these days. With the many areas where there are service delivery activities now it is simply because we are going into an election and people think it's a better time to be able to raise their grievances and their dissatisfaction about services that they are receiving from government.
V/O
Promises are made; municipal Councillors come and go, but in the end improvement is not evident for residents. We asked the Ehlanzeni District Municipality for comment, but despite numerous phone calls and emails, they remained silent.
AndrÉ Duif
We serve 98% international guests and if they come 10,000 kms and they can't go to the Panorama route it's a problem.
V/O
Andre Duif runs a guesthouse in the leafy suburbs of Hazyview.
Andre Duif
We need people that say enough is enough, we need corrupt officials to get out and bring new ones in, to look after, not only the area but our tourists and also the locals.
Eva Wagner
We've had to cancel a number of Panorama tours because for us obviously the safety of the guest is paramount. Sometimes the people are only here for two or three days, so you can't say we can't take you today we'll take you tomorrow. So they miss out on the whole experience that they planned and booked for in the Kruger Lowveld area.
Boy Johannes Nobunga
We spend most of our time trying to market and promote Mpumalanga as a preferred tourism destination, so if there are issues like service delivery, there are issues like mugging of tourists, crime in general, it sets us 2 or 3 steps back.
Andre Duif
Guests thats see this go home and they tell ten or twenty people. So that has a ripple effect all over the world, globally.
V/O
Duif, and other operators we spoke to, estimate that their bookings and inquiries have declined between 30 and 45%

Vincent Ramoba is a a tourism manager in the Hazyview area.
Vincent
People instead of coming down to Mpumalanga they'd rather go to the coast where there are no protests. Rather go to Cape Town, rather go to Durban, rather stay in Johannesburg... or rather budget and go to Botswana – there's the big 5 up there as well.
Lisa Sheard
Somebody fresh out of France or wherever where they might not seen is absolutely horrified at what they see and the fear, you can imagine as a first-time viewer of burning tyres and road blocks and that. How would you react? So, it instills fear in tourists and they don't want to come back or they want to go home and it also ruins their holiday.
Vincent
It's scary, it's really frightening and I don't think if you get such an experience you will ever think of coming back to South Africa.
V/O
If, as a tourist, if you were lucky enough to escape the actual protest, you may still may still be inconvenienced...
Eva Wagner
Sometimes people don't get breakfast because the staff didn't arrive because they couldn't get to work because of the protests.
V/O
Tourism is a key employer in the Lowveld. Protests may hurt the very residents that need the industry to thrive.
Lisa Sheard
For example if you take on the Panorama route, you've got Burke's Luck Potholes which is a famous place and all our overseas and domestic tourists go and visit there – Opposite is a village called Muramela. There's probably an 80% unemployment rate there. But of those 20 that are employed I bet you anything that about 80% of those people are employed in tourism. And that's the irony.
Boy Johannes Nobunga
CLAIRE: Is the community aware that these service delivery protests are affecting tourism so badly.

If they were aware I wouldn't think we'd be having the problem we're having, I wouldn't think we'd be having the concern we are having. The level of appreciation of what tourism can do to solve the many problems they're having as a society is something that is of a challenge to us on an ongoing basis we need to educate them and educate them and educate them all the time.
Vincent
The communities, they're not fighting with us. They're trying to send the information to somebody else – of course is the government – that's why they feel the government failed them for such a long time. Which means the government itself should start doing their job properly.
Lisa
There is absolutely no doubt that communities are hugely frustrated with the level of service delivery in our area and that we have idle officials and politicians... not all of them, but enough that things don't work. And communities – and we're part of the community – we're getting mad!




PROMO 10”
The entire Mpumalanga Lowveld region is plagued by regular service delivery protests, impacting on tourism in the area – a source of revenue that many locals rely on.


PROMO 15”
Service delivery protests in the Mpumalanga Lowveld region is taking it's toll on tourism in the area.

UPSOUND EVA WAGNER
Tourism is under attack at the moment... the whole industry has been affected from the bottom right up.


PROMO 15”
Ongoing service delivery protests in the Mpumalanga Lowveld is resulting in a substantial decline in tourism to the area.

UPSOUND VINCENT
It's scary, it's really frightening and I don't think if you get such an experience you will ever think of coming back to South Africa.


PROMO 30”
The Mpumalanga Lowveld is one of South Africa's prime tourist destinations, but regular service delivery protests and the barricading of key tourist routes is disrupting the entire industry.

UPSOUND EVA WAGNER
Sometimes people don't get breakfast because the staff didn't arrive because they couldn't get to work because of the protests.

What is needed to create a win-win situation for everyone?

Carte Blanche HD Nikola Vrahimis 21 September 2018 Script: LOWVELD TOURISM UNDER THREAT LINK This is the Mpumalanga Lowveld, known for it's forestry, agriculture like citrus and macadamia and of course it's tourism. V/O The Lowveld is served by the District Municipality of Ehlanzeni that covers four local municipalities – its seat is Mbombela. Tourists come for the iconic Kruger National Park, private game reserves and the Panorama Route that include jewels like Bourke's Luck Potholes, the Blyde River Canyon and God's Window. Lisa Sheard Tourism is very important to Mpumalanga and especially in our region, which is the Kruger/Lowveld-Ehlanzeni region, which contributes about 54% of the tourism GDP to Mpumalanga. V/O An estimated 1,5 million foreign tourists visited the province in 2017, says the executive director for tourism at the Kruger Lowveld Chamber of Business and Tourism, Lisa Sheard. Lisa Sheard Our primary markets are the traditional international markets like the UK, Germany.. the US is also a big market. So, a traditional South African inbound international market that visit our area. LINK This is God's Window. Tourists come from all over the world flock to come see this glorious splendour. Now imagine travelling all this way and getting to Graskop and not being able to get here because the road is blocked. V/o The entire Lowveld has been affected by service delivery protests. Roads have been blocked with branches, rocks and burning tyres. Dissatisfaction over poor service delivery lies at the heart of the unrest. Since the beginning of the year the frequency of protests has escalated, with demonstrators barricading roads along the scenic Panorama route, preventing residents and tourists from accessing places like Hazyview, the Blyde River Canyon, various local airports, and even the Kruger National Park. Eva Wagner Tourism is under attack at the moment... It's not just two or three vehicles that couldn't get to the Panorama, the whole industry has been affected from the bottom right up. V/O Eva Wagner owns a local one-stop tourism service that represents more than thirty operators and promotes over a hundred different activities in the area. Everyone has been impacted by the protests. Eva Wagner These are desperate measures. These people just don't know where to go anymore, they have found that if they protest in this way somebody will come and listen to them. LINK Service delivery protests here in Ka-Nyamazane just outside Mbombela started earlier this year after a hailstorm caused extensive damage to approximately 2000 houses. Three months later and the area is still dotted with blue plastic sheeting that's on top of the houses that still need to be fixed. V/O After first agreeing to be interviewed, activist leaders and community representatives withdrew their participation, but the Provincial Head of the Human Settlements department agreed to explain the background to the residents’ dissatisfaction. Kebone Masange Just over 2,000 houses were affected and most of them were asbestos houses which were roofed with asbestos,... And then those that were severely damaged, I'm talking about those that were huge openings and all that, there were about 450. CLAIRE: Right now, today, how many houses have been repaired? Do we have a number. Yes, we, we, have. The reports that I have is that 240 houses so far have been repaired. V/o What started out as protests about hail-damaged houses has escalated into something bigger over the last few months. Although the City of Mbombela has made funds available to assist, and the Provincial Government is on target to repair the worst-affected houses by the end of September, it seems promises are not enough to keep protests at bay. Kebone Masange But as you know the issues of employment and all that they are so much in our communities and people are actually scrambling for fewer job opportunities and work opportunities that come into this place. And due to that you end up having various interests playing in, and those who are not, disgruntled who are not chosen by this person... feeling like they've been sidelined. But that happens everywhere you go. Then unfortunately as a department we're not able to control that unless it comes up and then we intervene to try and cool temperatures and make the situation normal. Protest action across the Lowveld has a far-reaching impact. BJ Nobunga is the the CEO of the Mpumalanga Tourism and Parks Agency, or MTPA which coordinates tourism promotion in the Province – a responsibility that begins with local government. Boy Johannes Nobunga Service delivery has turned into something which is common in South Africa these days. With the many areas where there are service delivery activities now it is simply because we are going into an election and people think it's a better time to be able to raise their grievances and their dissatisfaction about services that they are receiving from government. V/O Promises are made; municipal Councillors come and go, but in the end improvement is not evident for residents. We asked the Ehlanzeni District Municipality for comment, but despite numerous phone calls and emails, they remained silent. AndrÉ Duif We serve 98% international guests and if they come 10,000 kms and they can't go to the Panorama route it's a problem. V/O Andre Duif runs a guesthouse in the leafy suburbs of Hazyview. Andre Duif We need people that say enough is enough, we need corrupt officials to get out and bring new ones in, to look after, not only the area but our tourists and also the locals. Eva Wagner We've had to cancel a number of Panorama tours because for us obviously the safety of the guest is paramount. Sometimes the people are only here for two or three days, so you can't say we can't take you today we'll take you tomorrow. So they miss out on the whole experience that they planned and booked for in the Kruger Lowveld area. Boy Johannes Nobunga We spend most of our time trying to market and promote Mpumalanga as a preferred tourism destination, so if there are issues like service delivery, there are issues like mugging of tourists, crime in general, it sets us 2 or 3 steps back. Andre Duif Guests thats see this go home and they tell ten or twenty people. So that has a ripple effect all over the world, globally. V/O Duif, and other operators we spoke to, estimate that their bookings and inquiries have declined between 30 and 45% Vincent Ramoba is a a tourism manager in the Hazyview area. Vincent People instead of coming down to Mpumalanga they'd rather go to the coast where there are no protests. Rather go to Cape Town, rather go to Durban, rather stay in Johannesburg... or rather budget and go to Botswana – there's the big 5 up there as well. Lisa Sheard Somebody fresh out of France or wherever where they might not seen is absolutely horrified at what they see and the fear, you can imagine as a first-time viewer of burning tyres and road blocks and that. How would you react? So, it instills fear in tourists and they don't want to come back or they want to go home and it also ruins their holiday. Vincent It's scary, it's really frightening and I don't think if you get such an experience you will ever think of coming back to South Africa. V/O If, as a tourist, if you were lucky enough to escape the actual protest, you may still may still be inconvenienced... Eva Wagner Sometimes people don't get breakfast because the staff didn't arrive because they couldn't get to work because of the protests. V/O Tourism is a key employer in the Lowveld. Protests may hurt the very residents that need the industry to thrive. Lisa Sheard For example if you take on the Panorama route, you've got Burke's Luck Potholes which is a famous place and all our overseas and domestic tourists go and visit there – Opposite is a village called Muramela. There's probably an 80% unemployment rate there. But of those 20 that are employed I bet you anything that about 80% of those people are employed in tourism. And that's the irony. Boy Johannes Nobunga CLAIRE: Is the community aware that these service delivery protests are affecting tourism so badly. If they were aware I wouldn't think we'd be having the problem we're having, I wouldn't think we'd be having the concern we are having. The level of appreciation of what tourism can do to solve the many problems they're having as a society is something that is of a challenge to us on an ongoing basis we need to educate them and educate them and educate them all the time. Vincent The communities, they're not fighting with us. They're trying to send the information to somebody else – of course is the government – that's why they feel the government failed them for such a long time. Which means the government itself should start doing their job properly. Lisa There is absolutely no doubt that communities are hugely frustrated with the level of service delivery in our area and that we have idle officials and politicians... not all of them, but enough that things don't work. And communities – and we're part of the community – we're getting mad! PROMO 10” The entire Mpumalanga Lowveld region is plagued by regular service delivery protests, impacting on tourism in the area – a source of revenue that many locals rely on. PROMO 15” Service delivery protests in the Mpumalanga Lowveld region is taking it's toll on tourism in the area. UPSOUND EVA WAGNER Tourism is under attack at the moment... the whole industry has been affected from the bottom right up. PROMO 15” Ongoing service delivery protests in the Mpumalanga Lowveld is resulting in a substantial decline in tourism to the area. UPSOUND VINCENT It's scary, it's really frightening and I don't think if you get such an experience you will ever think of coming back to South Africa. PROMO 30” The Mpumalanga Lowveld is one of South Africa's prime tourist destinations, but regular service delivery protests and the barricading of key tourist routes is disrupting the entire industry. metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): Tourism in our iconic Mpumalanga Lowveld is under threat!
metadata.Unique Selling Point: The issue has largely been kept out of the media but there are daily service delivery protests in the Ehlanzeni District Municipality area (basically the entire Lowveld region), threatening the livelihood of tourism in this area. Specifically, the Thaba Chweu Local Municipality has a bad reputation when it comes to service delivery (according to locals). So locals are barricading the scenic routes and access roads to major tourist attractions which means that tourism operators have to make last-minute changes to their itineraries and self-drive tourists are affected on a daily basis. Locals are protesting poor (or non-existent) service delivery. Outside Mbombela a community was hard hit by a hail storm and the repairs have not been done completely. Resident are angry and keep barricading the N4 and other major routes outside the city. Near Hazyview, communities are protesting lack of water and electricity. Some people were given RDP housing, but there has been no water or electricity connections and the community is fed-up. It's been 3 years now. So, hence the frustrations. Similarly Graskop communities are also desperate for water and sanitation services and they are barricading roads leading to the iconic God's Window. The whole area is plaqued by protests, but it is not one specific issue... The problem lies, it seems with the local and district municipalities and their total lack of service delivery. Schools are falling apart, hospitals are substandard, roads have massive potholes. Tourism is not the target per se, but it is one sector of business that is suffering greatly at the moment. Another opinion comes from the African National Chamber of Commerce & Industry Mpumalanga -- saying that politicians with ambitions have seen the opportunity and are instigating the protests. He says the protests are well organised and are as a result of the in-fighting between various factions within the ANC that want control over the province.
metadata.Summary: It is labelled as one of South Africa's most scenic areas. The Lowveld & Panorama Route of Mpumalanga showcases the natural awe inspiring areas of the district including God’s Window, Mac Mac Falls, Bourke’s Luck potholes, Kruger National Park and others. The area falls under the Ehlanzeni district municipality which encompasses four local municipalities -- Thaba Chweu, Bushbuckridge, City of Mbombela & Nkomazi. The entire area is affected by what started as locals protesting poor service delivery, and which has now escalated in to a more organised form of disruption with the aim of... no one knows for sure. Whilst National Government sees the area's tourism potential, the breakdown seems to be with local municipalities not coming to the party. But poor service delivery in the area has left local residents frustrated and they have now taken to daily protests, blockading the major scenic routes in the area, cutting off access to some of the tourist attractions. Although tourism is not the sole focus, many local tourism establishments that cater especially for international visitors are feeling the pressure as they have reported a decline in bookings (30 to 45%) over the past year. At least 2 international tourism operators are considering halting trips to the area for fear of safety, and because of the daily struggle to get tourists to and from Kruger National Park and airports, and other tourist destinations. Even roads to airports are affected. We speak to local accommodation owners and tourism operators about their daily frustrations and the disappointment of tourists when they are unable to visit the area's jewels. The roads affected seem to be the ones that lead to the major tourist destinations, eg entry to Kruger National Park, Burke's Luck, Graskop and even the Adventura Resort. Locals burn tyres, and barricade the roads with branches and rocks.
metadata.Further information: On 2nd July 2018, UNESCO declared the Barberton-Makhonjwa Mountainlands as South Africa's 10th World Heritage Site and Mpumalanga’s first! And on Friday 24 August Minister Derek Hanekom will open the new Graskop Gorge Lift in an ongoing effort to boost tourism in the Panorama Route area of the Lowveld, however whilst government and many local tourism organisations are serious about the region's tourism potential and the income it generates, the success of the region's tourism is hampered by a lack of service delivery from the local municipalities. Residents are protesting poor service delivery and various on-going issues on a daily basis in the area and this is affecting tourism throughout the region. Ehlanzeni District Municipality (EDM) is one of the three districts in Mpumalanga Province and is located in the Northern Eastern part covering the whole Southern part of the Kruger National Park. EDM covers an area of 27 895.47 km² which is about (36.47%) of the 76 495 km² which is the total estimated land size of Mpumalanga Province. The Thaba Chweu local municipality encompasses towns like Graskop, Pilgrims Rest and Sabie. Besides macadamia nut and citrus farming, tourism is the main source of income for many. South Africa has been named the top Adventure Tourism Destination for 2018, and Mpumalanga, Kruger and the Panorama route features strongly on the SA Tourism menu (after Cape Town). The area offers many activities for the adventure seeking tourist, from safari's at one of the many private, provincial or national reserves, abseiling, quadbiking, hiking, river rafting... the list goes on and on. National Accommodation Association of South Africa chair, Rosemarie van Staden says the area is feeling the pressure from cancellations by tourists and especially international tourism operators. It is not just the isolated B&B that is suffering. The whole region's economy is under threat. The Kruger Lowveld Chamber of Business and Tourism is concerned about the effect on all businesses if tourism would to dry up. The area is also becoming a crime hotspot. There are incidents of rock throwing at cars and people being attacked of threatened on some of the smaller roads. Protests outside Mbombela -- KaNyamazane -- started when RDP houses (about 35) were damaged by hail. The contractor hired by the municipality to fix the roofs of the houses affected was the first point of contention. Residents claim the process was not above board. Then once the contractor completed the repairs of 10 houses, their invoice to the City of Mbombela was R90,000 per roof, instead of the R45,000 estimated. The city refused to pay and the contractor stopped work. Locals were angry and started protesting. However, then things changed and a list of other (older) grievances were added to their list of demands. The mayor visited the area and tried to speak to the community and was chased away. Then the MEC of the province visited and was chased away. Insiders point to a more sinister cause behind the ongoing protests. Key politicians within the ANC are said to instigate communities into protesting, in an effort to win political ground. It's a fight between different factions within the ANC, fighting for control of the province... or so say insiders. In the meantime the entire Lowveld business community is struggling and desperate to find a way forward.
